title: Warm Up Protocol - Route Climbing
texts: An easy to follow warm up routine before route climbing
Start nice and easy - finish breathing heavily
15 controlled forward circles and 15 controlled backward circles
Start nice and easy - finish breathing heavily
15 controlled forward circles and 15 controlled backward circles
Use a theraband or light weights
Nice and easy climbing building the intensity slowly
Use a variety of grip positions - Start at a low intensity
Harder climbing providing some level of pump
Nice and easy climbing building the intensity slowly
Use a variety of grip positions - Start at a low intensity
Harder climbing providing some level of pump

Step 1: Cardiovascular warm up
Step 2: Mobility
Step 3: Easy Climbing
Step 4: Finger recruitment
Step 5: Harder Climbing

Cardiovascular warm up
-Complete 5 minutes of a cardio exercise of your choice. Skipping with a rope or jogging a great option for this.

Mobility
-30 seconds of several movements to warm up your entire body
1-Arm swings are rotations with your arms in big circles
2-One Leg RDL require you to touch the ground whilst keeping a slight bend in the knee. 
3-Side lunges will really help warm up your legs. Make sure to stay low whilst moving side to side.
4-IYT with a theraband will start activating the stabilizing muscles around your shoulder girdle throughout a large range of movement
5-Plank twists activate core muscles whilst warming up your rotational mobility

Easy Climbing
-5 minutes of low intensity traversing, bouldering or very easy routes.
If you at a crag or using a training board, a good option is to keep your feet on the floor and move between comfortable holds.

Finger recruitment
-Several hangs of a fingerboard or holds on the wall to recruit the fingers and prepare them for different grip positions being used in climbing later on
Use a variety of grip positions including the type of holds you plan to use during the sessions. An example could be to complete 3 hangs on;
Open/drag grip positions, half crimps then full crimps.

Harder Climbing
A moderately pumpy route or traverse which is below your limit and ideally pre-practiced. You want to feel mildly pumped at the end of this climb.

Now you're ready to start training, on-sight climbing or begin the red point process.

PLEASE remember warm ups are a very individual practice. This workout is an easy to follow option that our coaches use on a regular basis. You should always work out what works best for you!
